decision: coturn added with network_mode: host, not this file's usual bridge+explicit-port-mapping style
why: coturn's own Docker docs say so explicitly: "use the host network directly (recommended, as Docker performs badly with large port ranges)" -- a TURN relay needs the whole min-port..max-port UDP range individually reachable, not just one port like every other service here
evidence: fetched github.com/coturn/coturn docker/coturn/README.md live; verified coturn 4.18.0 image entrypoint/CMD and 'turnserver -h' locally before writing compose config

decision: TURN relay port range 49152-65535, listener port 3478 (both overridable via TURN_MIN_PORT/TURN_MAX_PORT/TURN_PORT)
why: Matrix's and coturn's own documented defaults (RFC 5766 Section 6.2 for the range) -- no reason to deviate for a school-sized deployment
evidence: element-hq/synapse docs/setup/turn/coturn.md firewall section, fetched live

decision: TURN credentials use coturn's TURN REST API mode (use-auth-secret + static-auth-secret), not static long-term username/password
why: Synapse's turn_shared_secret mechanism requires this: Synapse mints a fresh, short-lived username/password pair per client (HMAC-SHA1 of a unix-ts-prefixed username over the shared secret) and coturn must validate that exact construction, not a fixed credential pair
evidence: verified live: GET /_matrix/client/v3/voip/turnServer with a real user's token returned non-empty uris/username/password/ttl only after this scheme was wired on both sides

decision: Removed a 'no-dtls' line from turnserver.conf that an earlier draft carried over from older coturn docs
why: coturn 4.18.0 (the version pinned here) removed that directive -- DTLS is opt-in via a separate --dtls flag that already defaults to off, so no-dtls is neither valid config syntax nor necessary; coturn logged a "Bad configuration format: no-dtls" warning and otherwise ignored it
evidence: confirmed against the exact pinned image's own 'turnserver -h' output, not assumed from generic docs

decision: coturn's turnserver.conf is chown'd to uid/gid 65534 ("nobody", the image's fixed runtime user) from inside a throwaway root container against a writable mount, then chmod 600
why: the compose service mounts the file read-only, so a container running under that mount can't chown/chmod it, and coturn's own Dockerfile USER means even a maintenance run defaults to uid 65534 -- world-readable (644) was the tempting shortcut but leaves a real secret readable by every local user; discovered live: a plain host-side chmod 600 (owned by the host user) made the file unreadable by uid 65534 and coturn silently fell back to defaults, binding every interface with no auth at all
evidence: live repro: "Cannot find config file" in docker logs rumi-coturn traced to a Permission denied read, confirmed with docker exec cat as uid 65534

decision: scripts/setup.sh now unconditionally restarts the synapse container after every homeserver.yaml patch (step 6), not just on first install
why: Synapse reads homeserver.yaml once at process start and does not hot-reload turn_uris/turn_shared_secret -- adding TURN config to an ALREADY-RUNNING synapse and only calling a plain compose 'up -d' (which no-ops on an unchanged container) left the client-server TURN endpoint returning an empty object even though the file on disk was correct
evidence: live repro: turnServer returned {} immediately after the homeserver.yaml patch, then real non-empty credentials immediately after adding an explicit synapse restart

decision: coturn is force-recreated (not just brought up) on every setup.sh run, same as element already was
why: turnserver.conf is rewritten in place every run (fresh secret file, same path/mount/image) -- a plain 'up -d' no-ops on an already-running container even though the mounted file's bytes changed, the same stale-bind-mount class of bug element's force-recreate already exists to fix
evidence: live repro: coturn ran 2+ minutes on a config it couldn't even read (see the chown row above) because the first 'up -d' after fixing the file did not restart the container

decision: coturn is explicitly NOT part of the "run two checkouts side by side" story (COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME/RUMI_CONTAINER_PREFIX)
why: network_mode: host means coturn's ports are real host-wide ports, not per-project-remapped like Synapse/Element's bridge+BIND_ADDR ports -- two checkouts both running coturn on the same host will collide on TURN_PORT and the relay range unless the second one sets different values
evidence: documented honestly in deploy/.env.example and docs/RUNBOOK.md rather than silently implying the existing side-by-side story covers it

decision: coturn ships no-tls (plaintext TURN/STUN) for this stage, DTLS already off by default -- documented as a known gap, not silently under-secured
why: real TLS needs coturn's own certificate (separate from Synapse/Element's, since a browser's WebRTC stack talks to coturn directly, not through Caddy) -- that's production-hardening work already tracked in issue #6, matching this stack's existing BIND_ADDR=127.0.0.1-by-default posture
evidence: docs/RUNBOOK.md's new Calls section states this explicitly rather than leaving it implicit
